# Adjudication Task — Chapter 612

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃612화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“나와.”
  6|
  7|착 가라앉은 목소리. 어둠 속에서 날카롭게 빛나는 눈동자.
  8|
  9|그러나 나는 대답하는 대신 침착하게 그를 지켜봤다. 잠깐의 침묵이 흐른 뒤 딸칵, 하는 소리와 함께 거실이 환해진다.
 10|
 11|스윽.
 12|
 13|조심스럽게 걸음을 옮긴 남자가 힘주어 재차 입을 열었다.
 14|
 15|“숨어 있는 거 다 알고 있으니까 나오라고. 너 내가 누군지 알아?”
 16|
 17|당연히 알고 있다. 그의 이름과 얼굴, 심지어는 나이와 고향까지. 집에 돌아오자마자 이런 짓을 할 줄은 몰랐지만.
 18|
 19|“좋아, 마지막이다. 셋 셀 때까지 안 나오면 내 친한 동생 부른다. 걔 엄청 세고 잘나가는 헌터야. 하나. 둘…….”
 20|
 21|셋까지 다 세고 나면 무슨 일이 벌어질까 궁금하긴 했지만, 이미 볼 장 다 본 마당에 더 지켜보는 것도 낯부끄럽다.
 22|
 23|나는 한숨처럼 입을 열었다.
 24|
 25|“설마 그 친한 동생이라는 사람이 나는 아니지?”
 26|
 27|“……!”
 28|
 29|“얼씨구. 맞나 보네.”
 30|
 31|충격으로 석상처럼 굳어 있던 남자, 진호 형이 부릅뜬 눈으로 나를 바라봤다.
 32|
 33|“뭐, 뭐야. 네가 왜 거기서 나와.”
 34|
 35|“어차피 부를 거, 알고 미리 왔다. 됐냐?”
 36|
 37|잠시 침묵하던 진호 형이 무거운 표정으로 입을 열었다.
 38|
 39|“어디서부터 어디까지 봤냐.”
 40|
 41|“나와, 할 때부터.”
 42|
 43|“아, 씨바…….”
 44|
 45|“멋있더라. 포스가 너무 지려서 나도 모르게 나올 뻔했잖아.”
 46|
 47|“지금 놀리냐?”
 48|
 49|“응.”
 50|
 51|한 치의 망설임도 없는 당당한 대답에 나를 빤히 노려보던 진호 형이, 문득 실소를 흘렸다.
 52|
 53|“새끼. 하나도 안 변했네.”
 54|
 55|별것 없어 보이는 저 한 마디에, 이토록 반갑고 고마운 기분이 드는 것은 왜일까. 나는 그를 따라 웃으며 대답했다.
 56|
 57|“배고프다. 라면 끓여 줘.”
 58|
 59|
 60|
 61|* * *
 62|
 63|
 64|
 65|김이 모락모락 나는 냄비를 사이에 두고 마주 앉으니, 일 년 전쯤으로 돌아온 기분이다.
 66|
 67|물론 지금은 나도, 진호 형도 그때와는 많이 달라졌지만.
 68|
 69|“형이 정장 입은 건 처음 보네. 맨날 누더기 같은 추리닝만 걸치고 다니더니.”
 70|
 71|“인마, 누더기 같다니. 그거 꽤 비싼 메이커야.”
 72|
 73|“언제 샀는데?”
 74|
 75|“음. 고등학교 때?”
 76|
 77|진호 형이 몇 살이었더라. 잠깐 생각하던 내가 고개를 끄덕였다.
 78|
 79|“누더기 같은 게 아니라 누더기였네. 나 물 좀. 아니다. 혹시 소주 있어?”
 80|
 81|“차라리 고깃집에 가서 고기 있냐고 물어봐라.”
 82|
 83|“……보아하니 곧 단명하겠구만.”
 84|
 85|“김 계장 그 새끼만 아니었어도 진작 끊었다. 그 시발롬은 나이 차이도 얼마 안 나면서 사사건건 시비 걸고 지랄이야.”
 86|
 87|넥타이를 거칠게 풀어헤친 진호 형은 소주 석 잔을 연거푸 들이켰다.
 88|
 89|작년 말, 드디어 오랫동안 준비했던 공무원 시험에 합격한 그였다.
 90|
 91|“그래도 형이 공무원이 되긴 하네. 세상 참 말세다.”
 92|
 93|“이 새끼 말본새 보소. 그럼 안 될 줄 알았냐?”
 94|
 95|“아니. 되는 건 둘째치고 난 형이 조만간 야동 보다가 복상사할 줄 알았지.”
 96|
 97|“……음. 제법 일리가 있는 말이긴 한데.”
 98|
 99|부정하지 않는 걸 보니 그나마 아직 한 줄기 양심은 남아있군.
100|
101|만약 정부 정식 부처 중에 야동부가 있었다면 장관까지 올라가고도 남을 인간이다.
102|
103|야동부 차관직에 소라 아오이, 대변인으로는 키라라 아스카를 두고 폰허브를 호령했겠지.
104|
105|하지만 애석하게도 그런 정신 나간 부처는 존재하지 않았고, 특채 시험을 통해 합격한 진호 형은 알짜배기로 소문난 헌터 및 게이트 관리 부서에 발령 났다.
106|
107|물론 나와의 개인적인 친분이 보이지 않는 가산점을 부여했다는 것은 나도 내심 짐작하는 바였다.
108|
109|꼴꼴꼴.
110|
111|소주 잔을 가득 채운 진호 형이 불쑥 입을 열었다.
112|
113|“그런데 웬일이냐?”
114|
115|“잊으셨나 본데, 여기 내 집이야. 지금은 쓰레기 처리장인지 오피스텔인지 헷갈리긴 하지만.”
116|
117|“집주인이 두세 달 넘게 코빼기도 안 비추니까 하는 소리 아냐, 인마.”
118|
119|“그거라면 뭐 형 얼굴도 볼 겸해서 왔지. 가져갈 물건도 있었고.”
120|
121|“가져갈 물건? 옷 말하는 거면 그냥 하나 사지 그러냐. 돈도 썩어 나는 놈이.”
122|
123|“돈이 있어도 못 사. 파는 곳이 없어서.”
124|
125|“그런 게 어디 있어?”
126|
127|의아한 표정으로 되묻던 진호 형이 이내 짧은 탄성을 흘렸다.
128|
129|“아. 혹시 그 고물 캡슐?”
130|
131|“응, 그거. 다행히 안 버렸더라.”
132|
133|“버리면 죽여 버린다며.”
134|
135|“그래서 다행인 거지. 버렸으면 진짜 죽였을 텐데, 휴.”
136|
137|“……농담이지? 농담이라고 해 줘, 제발.”
138|
139|맨 처음 나를 무림으로 인도했던 게임 캡슐은 별다른 쓸모 없이 이곳에 방치되어 있었다.
140|
141|시스템이 허락한 덕분에 캡슐이 없어도 자유자재로 로그인과 로그아웃을 할 수 있게 되었으니까.
142|
143|하지만 그렇다 해서 애물단지 취급할 수는 없는 법이다.
144|
145|그 고물 캡슐이야말로 지금의 나를 만들어 준 일등 공신이며, 가치를 매길 수 없는 보물이니까.
146|
147|“내가 식탁은 안 닦아도 그 캡슐은 일주일에 한 번씩 닦는다. 그런데 그거 여전히 작동 안 되던데. 뭐 하러 가져가?”
148|
149|“그냥. 장식용이지, 뭐.”
150|
151|“귀신 들린 물건 아니냐? 전에 왜, 희망 고시원 살았을 때 네가 저 캡슐에서 잤다가 이상한 악몽 꿨다고…….”
152|
153|그러고 보니 그랬던 적이 있었지.
154|
155|처음 로그아웃했을 때의 이야기를 꺼내는 진호 형의 모습에, 나는 황급히 화제를 돌렸다.
156|
157|“혹시 그 뉴스 봤어? 이번에 중동이랑 아프가니스탄 쪽 난리 났던데.”
158|
159|“어? 갑자기 그 얘기를 왜 꺼내?”
160|
161|“아니, 봤냐고.”
162|
163|“당연히 보기야 봤지. 어제 중동 테러 단체랑 아프가니스탄 반군 세력들이 공동 성명서도 발표했잖아. 앞으로 테러 자제하고 밑에 놈들 단속 잘하겠다고. 사실상 쫄아서 항복 선언 한 거지.”
164|
165|“안심하면 안 돼. 어차피 잠깐일 테니까.”
166|
167|“그래도 진짜 대단한 사람들 아니냐? 그 이상한 복면 쓴 5인조.”
168|
169|다행히 화제 돌리기는 그럭저럭 먹혀 든 모양이다. 나는 내심 안도의 한숨을 내쉬며 고개를 끄덕였다.
170|
171|“그렇지.”
172|
173|“뭐, 어쨌든.”
174|
175|후루룩 면발을 빨아들인 진호 형이 소주로 입가심을 하며 말을 이었다.
176|
177|“고생 많았다. 새해 밝자마자 몬스터 웨이브에, 몬스터보다 더한 인간에, 이젠 사막이랑 아프리카까지 다녀오고.”
178|
179|“뭘 또 고생씩이나. 그냥 해야 할 일이니까 한 것…….”
180|
181|순간 멈칫한 나는 말꼬리를 흐렸다. 잠깐만. 이 인간이 지금 무슨 말을 하는 거야.
182|
183|“아니, 뭐라고?”
184|
185|“뭐긴 뭐야. 네가 들은 대로지. 혹시나 해서 찍어 봤는데 대충 맞았네.”
186|
187|“……!”
188|
189|“인마. 전 세계에 그럴 만한 짓을 할 사람이 몇 명이나 있다고. 다들 테러리스트 죽어 버렸으면 좋겠다. 반군 새끼들 꼴도 보기 싫다. 하면서도 막상 복면 뒤집어쓰고 실행에 옮길 사람이 누가 있겠냐? 아니, 애초에 그걸 실현할 수 있는 능력이 없지, 능력이.”
190|
191|눈을 동그랗게 뜬 내 모습에 진호 형이 피식 웃었다.
192|
193|“몇몇 사람들도 내심 짐작하면서도 쉬쉬하고 있을걸. 어차피 증거도 없는 데다가 탓할 일도 아니니까. 다만 어떤 말단 공무원은 운 좋게 그 복면인이 어떤 성격인지도 알고, 라면도 끓여 먹는 사이라 이렇게 슬쩍 떠볼 수 있는 거고.”
194|
195|나는 왠지 모르게 얼얼해진 뒤통수를 어루만졌다.
196|
197|내가 유력한 용의자로 지목될 거라는 사실은 짐작했지만, 이렇게 어이없을 만큼 쉽게 걸려들 줄은 몰랐다.
198|
199|“나, 나 진짜 아닌데?”
200|
201|“그래. 뭐 그렇다고 치자. 그래서 언제 돌아온 거야?”
202|
203|“…….”
204|
205|젠장. 이미 나가리다. 한숨을 푹 내쉰 나는 소주잔을 채우며 대답했다.
206|
207|“사흘. 아니다, 나흘 전.”
208|
209|“좋아. 이제 좀 고분고분해졌군.”
210|
211|“어디 가서 입 벙긋하지 마. 기밀인 건 둘째치고, 그때는 형이 위험해져.”
212|
213|나나 최 팀장. 그리고 가족들은 늘 보이지 않는 경호에 둘러싸여 있지만, 진호 형은 아니다.
214|
215|내 말의 의미를 찰떡처럼 알아들은 진호 형이 입맛을 다셨다.
216|
217|“으음. 뭔가 거물이 된 기분인데.”
218|
219|“거물이 되기 전에 폭발물이 먼저 배달 올지도 몰라.”
220|
221|“글쎄. 걔들은 다 알아도 나 못 건드릴걸? 진태경이 빡 돌면 무슨 일 벌일지 모르니까. 캬, 이거야말로 언터처블(Untouchable) 아니냐?”
222|
223|태평하게 웃은 진호 형이 말을 이었다.
224|
225|“그나저나 요새는 얼마나 바쁘게 지내길래, 언제 돌아왔는지도 헷갈려?”
226|
227|“음.”
228|
229|얼마나 바쁘냐고?
230|
231|어느덧 덥수룩하게 자란 턱수염을 긁적이던 내가 대답했다.
232|
233|“그냥 밤낮없이 훈련해. 가족들이랑 같이 식사하고, 계속해서 다시 훈련.”
234|
235|“훈련? 너 정도씩이나 되는 놈이 왜 훈련을 해?”
236|
237|“형은 명문대 나왔는데도 십 년 가까이 또 공부만 했잖아. 비슷한 거지.”
238|
239|“이 새끼가 아픈 곳을 찌르네. 그리고 너랑 나랑 같냐? 분야 차이가 아니라 아예 노는 레벨이 다른데.”
240|
241|그것도 그렇다. 진호 형이 나온 명문대는 연간 수백 명이 입학하고, 그와 비슷한 숫자가 졸업하니까.
242|
243|하지만 지금의 내게도 훈련은 필요했다.
244|
245|배움에는 끝이 없고, 공부(工夫)라는 단어는 학문에만 적용되는 것이 아니다.
246|
247|‘정확히는 새로운 뭔가를 배운다기보단, 천천히 되새긴다고 봐야겠지.’
248|
249|그런 의미에서 내가 하고 있는 훈련은 복습이라고 봐야 했다.
250|
251|나를 위한 공부이기도 하고, 이 세상을 위한 공부이기도 했다.
252|
253|아쉽게도 아직 완전한 결과물을 만들지는 못했지만.
254|
255|“으, 표정 진지한 거 봐. 뺨 한 대만 치고 싶다.”
256|
257|“……거, 한창 진지한데 그 아가리를 좀.”
258|
259|“입장 바꿔서 한번 생각해 봐라. 너 같으면 어떨지.”
260|
261|“음. 그건 그렇네. 한잔해.”
262|
263|우리는 사이좋게 술잔을 부딪쳤다. 소주를 한입에 털어 넣고, 다 식어 버린 면발을 뒤적거리던 진호 형이 묻는다.
264|
265|“그래서, 훈련은 잘 되어 가고?”
266|
267|“그럭저럭. 한 달쯤 전부터 준비했던 거라 슬슬 마무리 단계긴 한데…… 이게 쉽지가 않네.”
268|
269|이건 결코 엄살이 아니다.
270|
271|지금의 나는 마치 1만 피스로 이루어진 퍼즐을 맞춰야 하는 어린아이와 같았다.
272|
273|하나하나를 확인하고 짜 맞추는 과정에서 스스로에 대한 아쉬움과 부족함을 느꼈고, 이제는 마지막 남은 한 조각을 찾지 못해 어둠 속을 더듬거리고 있다.
274|
275|그리고 내 눈 앞을 가린 이 어둠의 이름을, 나는 이미 알고 있었다.
276|

“A few other people have probably guessed, but they’re keeping it to themselves. There’s no proof, and it’s not like they’d blame you. One low-ranking civil servant happens to know what that masked man is like, though. He even makes him ramyeon. So he can sound him out.”

[P88]
I rubbed the back of my head, which somehow felt numb.

[P89]
I’d expected to be a prime suspect. I hadn’t expected to give myself away so easily.

[P90]
“I-I’m really not him.”

[P91]
“Sure. Let’s say you aren’t. When did you get back?”

[P92]
“……”

[P93]
Damn it. There was no saving this.

[P94]
I sighed, filled my soju glass, and answered. “Three days ago. No, four.”

[P95]
“Good. Now you’re cooperating.”

[P96]
“Don’t tell anyone. Never mind that it’s classified—you’d be in danger.”

[P97]
Team Leader Choi, my family, and I were always surrounded by protection no one could see. Jin-ho wasn’t.

[P98]
He understood what I meant immediately and smacked his lips.

[P99]
“Hmm. I feel like a big shot.”

[P100]
“You might get a bomb delivered before you become one.”

[P101]
“I don’t know. Even if those guys find out, they won’t dare touch me. Who knows what Jin Taekyung would do if he lost his shit? Hah! Now *that’s* what I call Untouchable.”

[P102]
Jin-ho laughed without a care, then asked, “Anyway, how busy have you been? You can’t even remember when you got back.”

[P103]
“Hmm.”

[P104]
How busy?

[P105]
I scratched at the beard that had grown thick before I knew it.

[P106]
“I train day and night. Eat with my family, then train some more.”

[P107]
“Train? Why does someone at your level need to train?”

[P108]
“You graduated from a prestigious university and still spent nearly ten more years studying. Same thing.”

[P109]
“You bastard, going straight for the sore spot. Besides, how are we the same? It’s not just a different field—we’re on completely different levels.”

[P110]
He had a point. His prestigious university admitted hundreds of students every year, and about as many graduated.

[P111]
But I still needed training.

[P112]
There was no end to learning, and *gongbu*—study—wasn’t limited to academics.

[P113]
*To be precise, I’m not learning something new. I’m slowly going back over what I already know.*

[P114]
In that sense, my training was a kind of review. Study for my own sake, and for the sake of this world.

[P115]
Unfortunately, I still hadn’t managed to bring it all together.

[P116]
“Ugh, look at that serious face. Makes me want to slap you.”

[P117]
“……I’m trying to think, so could you shut that mouth of yours?”

[P118]
“Put yourself in my shoes. What would you do?”

[P119]
“Hmm. Fair enough. Have a drink.”

[P120]
We clinked glasses. Jin-ho knocked back his soju, poked at the noodles that had gone cold, and asked, “So? Is the training going well?”

[P121]
“More or less. I started preparing about a month ago, so I’m nearly done, but… it’s not easy.”

[P122]
I wasn’t exaggerating.

[P123]
I felt like a child trying to assemble a ten-thousand-piece puzzle. As I examined each piece and fitted it into place, I kept seeing my own shortcomings. Now, unable to find the last piece, I was groping through the dark.

[P124]
And I already knew the name of the darkness obscuring my sight.

[P125]
*The heart demon.*

[P126]
The dark cloud over my heart refused to clear. My worries about the Murim and the modern world… and, more than anything, the last sight of Kim Hwajong kept returning to me.

[P127]
His voice had sounded as though it might fade at any moment. His eyes had slowly closed amid the blood-red snow.

[P128]
Maybe I hadn’t come here for the capsule after all. Maybe I’d come to find some comfort.

[P129]
Not with the family I loved or the companions at my side, but with a friend living his own life in a completely different world. Maybe I’d just wanted to clink glasses with him like we used to.

[P130]
*Yeah. That was it.*

[P131]
All at once, I felt more at ease.

[P132]
I hadn’t shaken off the heart demon entirely, but acknowledging everything that had happened—and everything that troubled me—lifted some of the weight from my heart.

[P133]
I also realized that I wasn’t where I needed to be.

[P134]
“I’m leaving.”

[P135]
“The ramyeon’s cold. I was going to make tofu kimchi to go with the drinks… Wait, now?”

[P136]
“Yeah. I remembered something I have to do. Drink by yourself.”

[P137]
“Are you crazy?”

[P138]
“No. I’m your landlord. Want to start paying rent this month?”

[P139]
Jin-ho’s fierce expression vanished. He bent deeply at the waist.

[P140]
“Get home safely, Boss.”

[P141]
“Will do.”

[P142]
I laughed quietly and headed for the front door. Behind me, Jin-ho called out in a rush.

[P143]
“Hey! What about the capsule?”

[P144]
“Next time. I’ll take it next time.”

[P145]
Even as I said it, I knew that next time, I might give him the same answer and leave the capsule where it was. I might come only to clink glasses with him, just as I had today.

[P146]
“All right. Hang in there, you bastard.”

[P147]
Someone’s quiet murmur reached my ears as I walked on.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.

- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.

“……You’re joking, right? Please tell me you’re joking.”

[P63]
The game capsule that had first led me to the Murim had sat here unused ever since the System allowed me to Login and Logout freely without it.

[P64]
But that didn’t make it a piece of junk I could toss aside. That old capsule had done more than anything else to make me who I was. It was priceless.

[P65]
“I don’t wipe the dining table, but I wipe that capsule down once a week,” Jin-ho said. “It still doesn’t work, though. Why take it?”

[P66]
“Just because. For decoration, I guess.”

[P67]
“Isn’t that thing haunted? Remember when you lived at Hope Goshiwon? You slept in it and had some weird nightmare…”

[P68]
Oh. That had happened, hadn’t it?

[P69]
Jin-ho was bringing up my first Logout. I hurried to change the subject.

[P70]
“Did you see the news? Things got pretty crazy in the Middle East and Afghanistan.”

[P71]
“Huh? Where did that come from?”

[P72]
“I’m asking if you saw it.”

[P73]
“Of course I did. Yesterday the Middle Eastern terrorist groups and the Afghan rebels even issued a joint statement. Said they’d refrain from terrorism and keep their men in line from now on. Basically surrendered because they got scared.”

[P74]
“Don’t let your guard down. It’ll only last a little while.”

[P75]
“Still, those five weirdos in masks are incredible, aren’t they?”

[P76]
The change of subject seemed to have worked. I breathed an inward sigh of relief and nodded.

[P77]
“They are.”

[P78]
“Anyway.” Jin-ho slurped up some noodles, washed them down with soju, and went on. “You’ve been through a lot. A monster wave right after the new year, people worse than monsters, and now the desert and Africa too.”

[P79]
“It wasn’t that much. I just did what needed doing…”

[P80]
I stopped mid-sentence.

[P81]
Wait. What the hell had he just said?

[P82]
“Sorry, what?”

[P83]
“What you heard. I took a shot in the dark, and it looks like I was more or less right.”

[P84]
“……!”

[P85]
“Come on. How many people in the world could do something like that? Everyone says they wish the terrorists would die and they never want to see those rebel bastards again. But who’d actually put on a mask and do something about it? More to the point, who *could*?”

[P86]
Jin-ho gave a quiet laugh at my wide-eyed stare.

[P87]
“A few other people have probably guessed, but they’re keeping it to themselves. There’s no proof, and it’s not like they’d blame you. One low-ranking civil servant happens to know what that masked man is like, though. He even makes him ramyeon. So he can sound him out.”

[P88]
I rubbed the back of my head, which somehow felt numb.

[P89]
I’d expected to be a prime suspect. I hadn’t expected to give myself away so easily.

[P90]
“I-I’m really not him.”

[P91]
“Sure. Let’s say you aren’t. When did you get back?”

[P92]
“……”

[P93]
Damn it. There was no saving this.

[P94]
I sighed, filled my soju glass, and answered. “Three days ago. No, four.”

[P95]
“Good. Now you’re cooperating.”

[P96]
“Don’t tell anyone. Never mind that it’s classified—you’d be in danger.”

[P97]
Team Leader Choi, my family, and I were always surrounded by protection no one could see. Jin-ho wasn’t.

[P98]
He understood what I meant immediately and smacked his lips.

[P99]
“Hmm. I feel like a big shot.”

[P100]
“You might get a bomb delivered before you become one.”

[P101]
“I don’t know. Even if those guys find out, they won’t dare touch me. Who knows what Jin Taekyung would do if he lost his shit? Hah! Now *that’s* what I call Untouchable.”

[P102]
Jin-ho laughed without a care, then asked, “Anyway, how busy have you been? You can’t even remember when you got back.”

[P103]
“Hmm.”

[P104]
How busy?

[P105]
I scratched at the beard that had grown thick before I knew it.

[P106]
“I train day and night. Eat with my family, then train some more.”

[P107]
“Train? Why does someone at your level need to train?”

[P108]
“You graduated from a prestigious university and still spent nearly ten more years studying. Same thing.”

[P109]
“You bastard, going straight for the sore spot. Besides, how are we the same? It’s not just a different field—we’re on completely different levels.”

[P110]
He had a point. His prestigious university admitted hundreds of students every year, and about as many graduated.

[P111]
But I still needed training.

[P112]
There was no end to learning, and *gongbu*—study—wasn’t limited to academics.

[P113]
*To be precise, I’m not learning something new. I’m slowly going back over what I already know.*

[P114]
In that sense, my training was a kind of review. Study for my own sake, and for the sake of this world.

[P115]
Unfortunately, I still hadn’t managed to bring it all together.

[P116]
“Ugh, look at that serious face. Makes me want to slap you.”

[P117]
“……I’m trying to think, so could you shut that mouth of yours?”

[P118]
“Put yourself in my shoes. What would you do?”

[P119]
“Hmm. Fair enough. Have a drink.”

[P120]
We clinked glasses. Jin-ho knocked back his soju, poked at the noodles that had gone cold, and asked, “So? Is the training going well?”

[P121]
“More or less. I started preparing about a month ago, so I’m nearly done, but… it’s not easy.”

[P122]
I wasn’t exaggerating.

[P123]
I felt like a child trying to assemble a ten-thousand-piece puzzle. As I examined each piece and fitted it into place, I kept seeing my own shortcomings. Now, unable to find the last piece, I was groping through the dark.

[P124]
And I already knew the name of the darkness obscuring my sight.

[P125]
*The heart demon.*

[P126]
The dark cloud over my heart refused to clear. My worries about the Murim and the modern world… and, more than anything, the last sight of Kim Hwajong kept returning to me.

[P127]
His voice had sounded as though it might fade at any moment. His eyes had slowly closed amid the blood-red snow.

[P128]
Maybe I hadn’t come here for the capsule after all. Maybe I’d come to find some comfort.

[P129]
Not with the family I loved or the companions at my side, but with a friend living his own life in a completely different world. Maybe I’d just wanted to clink glasses with him like we used to.

[P130]
*Yeah. That was it.*

[P131]
All at once, I felt more at ease.

[P132]
I hadn’t shaken off the heart demon entirely, but acknowledging everything that had happened—and everything that troubled me—lifted some of the weight from my heart.

[P133]
I also realized that I wasn’t where I needed to be.

[P134]
“I’m leaving.”

[P135]
“The ramyeon’s cold. I was going to make tofu kimchi to go with the drinks… Wait, now?”

[P136]
“Yeah. I remembered something I have to do. Drink by yourself.”

[P137]
“Are you crazy?”

[P138]
“No. I’m your landlord. Want to start paying rent this month?”

[P139]
Jin-ho’s fierce expression vanished. He bent deeply at the waist.

[P140]
“Get home safely, Boss.”

[P141]
“Will do.”

[P142]
I laughed quietly and headed for the front door. Behind me, Jin-ho called out in a rush.

[P143]
“Hey! What about the capsule?”

[P144]
“Next time. I’ll take it next time.”

[P145]
Even as I said it, I knew that next time, I might give him the same answer and leave the capsule where it was. I might come only to clink glasses with him, just as I had today.

[P146]
“All right. Hang in there, you bastard.”

[P147]
Someone’s quiet murmur reached my ears as I walked on.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.

I sighed, filled my soju glass, and answered. “Three days ago. No, four.”

[P95]
“Good. Now you’re cooperating.”

[P96]
“Don’t tell anyone. Never mind that it’s classified—you’d be in danger.”

[P97]
Team Leader Choi, my family, and I were always surrounded by protection no one could see. Jin-ho wasn’t.

[P98]
He understood what I meant immediately and smacked his lips.

[P99]
“Hmm. I feel like a big shot.”

[P100]
“You might get a bomb delivered before you become one.”

[P101]
“I don’t know. Even if those guys find out, they won’t dare touch me. Who knows what Jin Taekyung would do if he lost his shit? Hah! Now *that’s* what I call Untouchable.”

[P102]
Jin-ho laughed without a care, then asked, “Anyway, how busy have you been? You can’t even remember when you got back.”

[P103]
“Hmm.”

[P104]
How busy?

[P105]
I scratched at the beard that had grown thick before I knew it.

[P106]
“I train day and night. Eat with my family, then train some more.”

[P107]
“Train? Why does someone at your level need to train?”

[P108]
“You graduated from a prestigious university and still spent nearly ten more years studying. Same thing.”

[P109]
“You bastard, going straight for the sore spot. Besides, how are we the same? It’s not just a different field—we’re on completely different levels.”

[P110]
He had a point. His prestigious university admitted hundreds of students every year, and about as many graduated.

[P111]
But I still needed training.

[P112]
There was no end to learning, and *gongbu*—study—wasn’t limited to academics.

[P113]
*To be precise, I’m not learning something new. I’m slowly going back over what I already know.*

[P114]
In that sense, my training was a kind of review. Study for my own sake, and for the sake of this world.

[P115]
Unfortunately, I still hadn’t managed to bring it all together.

[P116]
“Ugh, look at that serious face. Makes me want to slap you.”

[P117]
“……I’m trying to think, so could you shut that mouth of yours?”

[P118]
“Put yourself in my shoes. What would you do?”

[P119]
“Hmm. Fair enough. Have a drink.”

[P120]
We clinked glasses. Jin-ho knocked back his soju, poked at the noodles that had gone cold, and asked, “So? Is the training going well?”

[P121]
“More or less. I started preparing about a month ago, so I’m nearly done, but… it’s not easy.”

[P122]
I wasn’t exaggerating.

[P123]
I felt like a child trying to assemble a ten-thousand-piece puzzle. As I examined each piece and fitted it into place, I kept seeing my own shortcomings. Now, unable to find the last piece, I was groping through the dark.

[P124]
And I already knew the name of the darkness obscuring my sight.

[P125]
*The heart demon.*

[P126]
The dark cloud over my heart refused to clear. My worries about the Murim and the modern world… and, more than anything, the last sight of Kim Hwajong kept returning to me.

[P127]
His voice had sounded as though it might fade at any moment. His eyes had slowly closed amid the blood-red snow.

[P128]
Maybe I hadn’t come here for the capsule after all. Maybe I’d come to find some comfort.

[P129]
Not with the family I loved or the companions at my side, but with a friend living his own life in a completely different world. Maybe I’d just wanted to clink glasses with him like we used to.

[P130]
*Yeah. That was it.*

[P131]
All at once, I felt more at ease.

[P132]
I hadn’t shaken off the heart demon entirely, but acknowledging everything that had happened—and everything that troubled me—lifted some of the weight from my heart.

[P133]
I also realized that I wasn’t where I needed to be.

[P134]
“I’m leaving.”

[P135]
“The ramyeon’s cold. I was going to make tofu kimchi to go with the drinks… Wait, now?”

[P136]
“Yeah. I remembered something I have to do. Drink by yourself.”

[P137]
“Are you crazy?”

[P138]
“No. I’m your landlord. Want to start paying rent this month?”

[P139]
Jin-ho’s fierce expression vanished. He bent deeply at the waist.

[P140]
“Get home safely, Boss.”

[P141]
“Will do.”

[P142]

[P143]
“Hey! What about the capsule?”

[P144]
“Next time. I’ll take it next time.”

[P145]
Even as I said it, I knew that next time, I might give him the same answer and leave the capsule where it was. I might come only to clink glasses with him, just as I had today.

[P146]
“All right. Hang in there, you bastard.”

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
